# A canvas-group e2e witness times out before the engine's 30 s bound

Owned by @neo-opus-ada, who wrote the witness (#19103, PR #19125). No curated labels: each sighting costs an unrelated PR a red e2e run and a rerun.

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/core/CanvasGroupPainting.spec.mjs` › "a group whose canvas worker fails to load fails alone, and a healthy group keeps painting" failed on CI three times, each time on a PR whose diff touches no canvas code, each time at the same assertion. Its 20 s poll for "the failed group's canvas component reports its worker as unavailable" stayed `false`:

| Date | PR | Run, shard | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-05 | #20317 | 42031233449, e2e-engine 1/4 | the same head passed it 3 of 3 locally (Vega) |
| 2026-11-17 | #21281 | 44155325970 attempt 2, 7/14 | the test ran 21.9 s; attempt 1 of that shard passed it (Vega) |
| 2026-11-18 | #21377 | 44362215591, 14/15 | the diff is calendar code and `e2eCiSelection.mjs` |

Observed: the poll times out on loaded runners and passes on retry and locally. Inferred, not measured: the engine's fast failure path did not deliver within 20 s on those runs. Whether the `error` event fired late, never, or its message raced is unknown.

## The Problem

The witness asserts that a failed canvas start is reported within 20 s. The engine reports it on one of two paths. The fast path: the canvas SharedWorker's `error` event makes `Manager` send `canvasStartFailed`, the group's waits fail, and `SharedCanvas` logs "canvas worker unavailable". The slow path is the silent-start bound, 30 s. When the fast path is late on a loaded runner, the engine still fails the group correctly at 30 s, after the witness has given up. A correct engine then reads as a red build.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/Manager.mjs` `createWorker()`: `worker.addEventListener('error', …)` sends `canvasStartFailed` for a canvas worker, "the only programmatic signal that a canvas worker failed to load or parse" (#19092).
- `src/worker/CanvasGroups.mjs`: `startBound: 30000`, with a timer per group that calls `fail(group, 'silent')`; `canvasStartFailed` calls `fail(group, 'load')`. `startError()` names the cause: "canvas worker of group … did not start (load|silent)".
- `src/app/SharedCanvas.mjs`: a rejected `startWorker` / `whenCanvasReady` logs `Neo.app.SharedCanvas: canvas worker unavailable` with that error.
- The witness points root B's `neomjs-canvas-worker-*` SharedWorkers at `/missing-canvas-worker.mjs` through an init script and polls the console and worker error lines with `timeout: 20000`.

Design authority: `CanvasGroups#startBound` — "Milliseconds a group may stay silent before its start counts as failed" (30000). The engine's guarantee for a failed start is that bound; the `error` event only makes it faster.

## The Fix

- The witness waits for what the engine guarantees: its poll covers `CanvasGroups#startBound`, read from the engine's source, plus a margin.
- The witness records which path reported the failure (`load` from the `error` event, or `silent` from the bound) and how long it took, so a slow fast path shows up as data on a green run instead of as a red one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The witness's poll covers the engine's silent-start bound plus a margin, and its failure message names the bound it covered.
- [ ] AC-2: A passing run records, as a test annotation, which path reported (`load` or `silent`) and after how long.
- [ ] AC-3: With root B's canvas worker loading but never answering (only the bound can report), the witness passes at head and fails on `dev`; the unmodified witness passes 10 of 10 under `--repeat-each=10`, and the PR's e2e run is green.

## Out of Scope

- The fast path's own latency on CI. If AC-2's annotations show `silent` on CI, that is a `Manager` follow-up with the measurement in hand.
- A canvas worker created at boot that fails to load still holding the root's boot (the defect-note recorded on PR #19125).

## Avoided Traps

- Retrying the test, or a CI-only timeout literal: it hides the path that was slow and restates a number the engine owns.
- Lowering `startBound` for the whole app: it changes production failure timing to suit a test.

## Related

- #19103 and PR #19125 (canvas worker per window group, the witness), #19092 (the load-error signal).
- Sightings: PR #20317, PR #21281, PR #21377.
